description: D-PACE master policy file — defines regex patterns, retention windows, classification rules, and legal mandate mappings.

classification_levels.name: Restricted
classification_levels.description: Highest sensitivity. Data whose unauthorised disclosure would cause severe harm. Includes PCI PANs, SSNs, health records.

classification_levels.name: Confidential
classification_levels.description: Sensitive internal data. Unauthorised disclosure would cause moderate harm. Includes internal emails, contract data.

classification_levels.name: Internal
classification_levels.description: Non-public data with limited sensitivity. Business documents not intended for external distribution.

classification_levels.name: Unclassified
classification_levels.description: No sensitive content detected. Public or trivially non-sensitive data.

regex_patterns.name: US Social Security Number
regex_patterns.description: Detects SSNs in plain text. Restricted under GDPR as special-category data.

regex_patterns.name: Payment Card PAN (Visa/MC/Amex/Discover)
regex_patterns.description: Detects unmasked Primary Account Numbers. Storage triggers PCI DSS Req 3.2 violation if not justified.

regex_patterns.name: Email Address
regex_patterns.description: Email addresses are personal data under GDPR Art. 4(1). Triggers data minimisation review.

regex_patterns.name: US Phone Number
regex_patterns.description: US phone numbers are personal data under GDPR.

regex_patterns.name: International Bank Account Number
regex_patterns.description: Bank account numbers. Restricted financial data.

regex_patterns.name: IPv4 Address
regex_patterns.description: IPv4 addresses may constitute personal data under GDPR when linkable to an individual.

regex_patterns.name: Date of Birth (common formats)
regex_patterns.description: Date of birth is sensitive personal data. Context-aware pattern (requires label).

regex_patterns.name: AWS Access Key ID
regex_patterns.description: AWS access key IDs in plaintext represent a critical credential exposure.

regex_patterns.name: PEM Private Key
regex_patterns.description: PEM private key header. Indicates cryptographic key material stored in plaintext.

retention_policies.description: Personal data must not be kept longer than necessary. Default 1-year window; shorter periods apply for specific categories.

retention_policies.mandate: PCI DSS v4.0 Req 9.4.3 — Cardholder Data Retention
retention_policies.description: Cardholder data (CHD) must be retained only as long as required by legal/business needs and disposed of securely.

retention_policies.mandate: NIST SP 800-53 SI-12 — Information Management and Retention
retention_policies.description: Organisations must manage and retain system-related information in accordance with applicable laws and policies.

classification_rules.name: No pattern matches → Internal (non-public) or Unclassified

NIST_SP_800_53.AC-1: Policy and procedures for access control — enforced by classification tags
NIST_SP_800_53.AC-3: Access enforcement — classification drives access decisions in downstream systems
NIST_SP_800_53.AU-2: Event logging — all scans and violations written to dpace.db audit tables
NIST_SP_800_53.AU-9: Protection of audit information — dpace.db should be on restricted volume
NIST_SP_800_53.CM-8: Information system component inventory — asset_inventory table fulfils this
NIST_SP_800_53.RA-2: Security categorisation — FIPS 199 levels mapped to classification_levels
NIST_SP_800_53.SA-8: Security/Privacy engineering principles — Privacy-by-design in scanner design
NIST_SP_800_53.SC-28: Protection of information at rest — Restricted files flagged for encryption review
NIST_SP_800_53.SI-12: Information management and retention — retention_auditor enforces SI-12 windows

PCI_DSS_v4.Req_3.1: Protect stored account data — CHD flagged Restricted; storage minimised
PCI_DSS_v4.Req_3.2: Do not retain sensitive authentication data — CREDIT_CARD_PAN pattern triggers violation
PCI_DSS_v4.Req_3.3: Protect primary account numbers (PAN) — PAN masking/storage violations logged
PCI_DSS_v4.Req_7.2: Least-privilege access model — classification informs access policy
PCI_DSS_v4.Req_9.4: Protect all media — Restricted physical/digital media flagged
PCI_DSS_v4.Req_10.2: Audit log events — scan_results and policy_violations serve as audit trail
PCI_DSS_v4.Req_12.3: Risk assessment — classification output feeds into risk register

GDPR.Art_4_1: Definition of personal data — all PII patterns map to Art. 4(1) personal data
GDPR.Art_5_1e: Storage limitation — retention_auditor checks against GDPR retention window
GDPR.Art_9: Special categories — SSN, DOB, health data classified Restricted
GDPR.Art_17: Right to erasure — policy_violations of type RETENTION_EXCEEDED support Art.17
GDPR.Art_25: Data protection by design — classification-at-discovery implements Art.25
GDPR.Art_30: Records of processing — asset_inventory + scan_results = Art.30 record
GDPR.Art_32: Security of processing — Restricted data triggers encryption/access review
GDPR.Art_83: Administrative fines context — violation severity aligns with Art.83 tiers
